definitions.definition: For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For 0<=alpha<=1, 0<=a<=b, b-a<=1, and f_j in L^infinity([a,b];H^alpha) with f_j' in L^infinity([a,b];H^(-23/14)), j=1,2,3, the operator Ctri_[a,b] obeys |Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)|_2<=c*(b-a)*product_j |f_j|_(Xsrc)+c*|f_i|_(L^infinity H^(-23/14))*product_(j!=i)|f_j|_(L^infinity L^2) for each i=1,2,3. If the three inputs are time-independent then |Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)|_2<=c_alpha*(b-a)^alpha*product_j |f_j|_(alpha). The constants are independent of a,b and the inputs.

For 0<gamma<=1 set a_gamma=1/2-gamma when gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 when gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 when gamma>1/2. Then a_gamma in [0,1), ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)). argument.text: Apply E003 on I=[a,b]. For the time-dependent assertion take its alpha=0: each smooth spatial path is in L^infinity L^2 and its piecewise derivative is in H^(-pstar); time continuity removes jump masses. The source allows each choice of negative-norm slot. For the time-independent assertion use arbitrary 0<=sigma<=1 as its alpha and constant H^sigma inputs, whose derivatives are zero. Put c0=sqrt(2*pi). Every source spatial norm and every source X norm is c0 times ours, so dividing its inequalities by c0 changes their constants by c0^2 and leaves all time powers and uniformities unchanged. This proves both normalized Ctri bounds, first for the stated paths and then by their bounded extensions.

argument.text: H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Define a_gamma as stated. E005 with source sigma=gamma, choosing endpoint epsilon=1/8 when gamma=1/2, gives the product estimate; division by c0 changes its constant by c0. The three cases give a_gamma in [0,1). The gamma=0 product case of E005 is not needed.

produces.statement: a_gamma is in [0,1) and ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)) for all such f,g.

argument.text: Fix a,tau,t,w,M0 and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Set wshift=S_a w. It is mean-zero and has the same H^gamma norm. From the definitions B_(a+r)(f,g)=S_(-a)B_r(S_a f,S_a g), hence Fstage_(a,t)(w)=S_(-a)Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift). Apply E004 with source n=0, timestep tau, s=t-a, sigma=gamma, f=g=wshift and beta=a_gamma; take epsilon=1/8 in the middle case. All are in its interval: beta0<=a_gamma<=1+gamma in each of the three cases. The exponents are (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma) for gamma<1/2, 11/17 for gamma=1/2, and (1+gamma)/2 for gamma>1/2. They are at least gamma: in the first case the numerator minus gamma times its denominator is 1/2-gamma/2+gamma^2>0; in the second 11/17>1/2; in the third 1>=gamma. Since tau<=1 these source powers are <=tau^gamma. Divide by c0 and use the S isometry to obtain the first stage bound.

Apply E004 again to the same wshift and time parameters with beta=1+gamma, which is the upper permitted endpoint. Its exponent is zero, giving ||Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma||wshift||_(H^gamma)^2 after the same norm conversion. Use the S isometry to obtain the uniform second bound. Discharge L1 and quantify the inputs and interval. With F001-F003 this proves the output assertion.
